newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-BASTIA AND BORDEAUX FIGHT TO STAY CLOSE TO LEADERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BASTIA AND BORDEAUX FIGHT TO STAY CLOSE TO LEADERS.

text.p: Bordeaux will be looking to keep surprise package Bastia in check when the two sides meet in a battle to stay in touch with leading pair Monaco and Paris Saint-Germain in the French first division on Thursday.

Bastia, who have coped remarkably well with the loss of playmaker Lubomir Moravcik through injury, are on 39 points, two in front of Bordeaux and six behind leaders Monaco, who like PSG are in action on Friday.

"They could have gone through a loss of form after the injury to Moravcik," said admiring Bordeaux coach Rolland Courbis on Wednesday. "But they have digested the absence of such an important player in a quite surprising manner."

Moravcik broke a leg in a tackle by Monaco defender Emmanuel Petit in a rough 0-0 draw at Bastia on October 12. The Slovakian international, who joined Bastia from relegated Saint-Etienne in the off-season, resumed light training this week.
Bastia picked up only one point in their following three matches. But since then they have won six games, including an away victory over champions Auxerre, and lost only once.

They were deprived of several first choice players through injury early last month but the team responded well when coach Frederic Antonetti said: "I want warriors. I expect proof that my squad is made up of a group that sweats."

Antonetti, who welcomes back his 11-goal striker Anton Drobnjak from World Cup duty with Yugoslavia, said: "I savour our present results for their true value. But I know that tomorrow we can just as easily go through a bad period.
"That's what pushes us to work, to progress without pause."
Drobnjak missed the 2-1 win at Lille on Saturday.

Bordeaux, who beat Rennes 2-0 at home last weekend, will be without suspended veteran striker Jean-Pierre Papin and possibly also injured Ibrahima Ba, the highly rated Dakar-born midfielder courted by Barcelona.
But France under-21 midfielder Johan Micoud should be back after injury.
"It's an end-of-stage match with all that that implies," said Courbis of the team's last game before the winter break, which lasts until January 25.
"We must make one last effort but Bastia's calculations will be the same as ours."
